title: Pictographs, Bar Graphs, Pie Charts and Line Graphs
seo_title: Grade 6 Representing Data Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_code: Grade 6: 5.2 Representing data; 5.3 Analysing, interpreting and reporting data
standard_text: Draw a variety of graphs to display and interpret data, including pictographs (many-to-one correspondence), bar graphs and double bar graphs; critically read and interpret data presented in a variety of ways, including pie charts; analyse data by answering questions related to data categories, data sources and contexts.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 graphs worksheets: pictographs, bar graphs, pie charts and line graphs. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Use the key and the scale.
key_sub: A pie chart shows parts of a whole.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • In a pictograph, the key tells you what one picture stands for.
  • In a bar graph, read the top of each bar against the scale.
  • A pie chart shows parts of a whole. A quarter of the circle is a quarter of the data (90°).
  • A line graph shows how something changes over time.

Examples

Example

A pie chart of 60 learners: soccer is half

half of 60

Answer: 30 learners

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Each picture as 1Use the key.
Reading the scaleCheck what each line is worth.
Parts of a pieThe whole circle is all the data.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about graphs?
faq.a: Draw and interpret pictographs, bar graphs and double bar graphs, and read and interpret pie charts and other graphs.

faq.q: When is a pie chart useful?
faq.a: To show parts of a whole.

faq.q: When is a line graph useful?

faq.a: It tells you what each picture stands for.

items.q: How many votes were there in all?
items.e: Step 1: read every bar: Spring 6, Summer 10, Autumn 12, Winter 5. Step 2: add them: 6 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 33 votes.

items.q: How many cups were sold in all?
items.e: Step 1: read every bar: Mon 30, Tue 5, Wed 20, Thu 10. Step 2: add them: 30 + 5 + 20 + 10 = 65 cups.

items.q: How many points did the teams score in all?
items.e: Step 1: read every bar: Tigers 15, Hawks 10, Bears 60, Lions 70. Step 2: add them: 15 + 10 + 60 + 70 = 155 points.

items.q: How many cans did the classes collect in all?
items.e: Step 1: read every bar: Room 1 20, Room 2 10, Room 3 35, Room 4 30. Step 2: add them: 20 + 10 + 35 + 30 = 95 cans.

items.q: How many more votes do the Yellow and Red bars show together than the Green bar?
items.e: Step 1: Yellow + Red = 65 + 40 = 105. Step 2: compare with Green (70): 105 − 70 = 35, so 35 more votes.

items.q: How many more learners do the Dog and Cat bars show together than the Hamster bar?
items.e: Step 1: Dog + Cat = 8 + 10 = 18. Step 2: compare with Hamster (12): 18 − 12 = 6, so 6 more learners.

items.q: How many more learners do the Bus and Bike bars show together than the Walk bar?
items.e: Step 1: Bus + Bike = 20 + 15 = 35. Step 2: compare with Walk (30): 35 − 30 = 5, so 5 more learners.

items.q: How many more books do the Space and Animals bars show together than the Sports bar?
items.e: Step 1: Space + Animals = 50 + 30 = 80. Step 2: compare with Sports (70): 80 − 70 = 10, so 10 more books.

items.q: How many learners did not choose pizza?
items.e: Step 1: add all the bars: 15 + 5 + 35 + 25 = 80. Step 2: take away Pizza (25): 80 − 25 = 55 learners. Or add the other three bars: 15 + 5 + 35 = 55.

items.q: How many days were not cloudy?
items.e: Step 1: add all the bars: 4 + 11 + 7 + 8 = 30. Step 2: take away Cloudy (11): 30 − 11 = 19 days. Or add the other three bars: 4 + 7 + 8 = 19.

items.q: How many books did Thandi read?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle stands for 1 book. The Thandi row has 4 circles, so it shows 4 books.

items.q: How many shells did Nomsa find?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle stands for 1 shell. The Nomsa row has 4 circles, so it shows 4 shells.
Look at the key: each star stands for 1 learner. Read every row: Dog 4, Fish 3, Bird 7, Guinea pig 2. Add them: 4 + 3 + 7 + 2 = 16 learners.
The key says one whole star = 2 learners. Half a star is half of 2, which is 1 learner.

items.q: Each star stands for 2 books. Dumisani read 12 books. How many stars should be in his row?
items.e: Count in 2s until you reach 12: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. That is 6 steps, so draw 6 stars. Check: 6 × 2 = 12. (Drawing 12 stars would show 12 × 2.)

items.q: Which row shows 7 votes?
items.e: Half a circle is 1, so 7 votes is 3 and a half circles. The Banana row has 3 circles and half a circle: 3 × 2 = 6, and half of 2 is 1, so 6 + 1 = 7 votes.

items.q: Which row shows the fewest learners?
items.e: Every square stands for the same number, so the row with the fewest squares shows the fewest. The Car row has 1 square: 1 × 2 = 2 learners.

items.q: How many more votes did Banana get than Watermelon?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle stands for 2 votes. Banana: 6 × 2 = 12 and Watermelon: 2 × 2 = 4. How many more means find the difference: 12 − 4 = 8 votes.

items.q: Each square stands for 5 learners. 35 learners walk to school. How many squares should be in the Walk row?
items.e: Count in 5s until you reach 35: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. That is 7 steps, so draw 7 squares. Check: 7 × 5 = 35. (Drawing 35 squares would show 35 × 5.)

items.q: Which row shows 25 cans?
items.e: Each circle = 5. 25 ÷ 5 = 5, so look for 5 circles. The 3C row has 5 circles: 5 × 5 = 25 cans.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar graph go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 1, 2, 3 … Each line is 1 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 1s.

items.q: How many families have 6 people?
items.e: The scale goes up in 1s. The column for 6 people ends on the line for 3. So the answer is 3 families.

items.q: How many more learners have a bird than a guinea pig?
items.e: The scale goes up in 1s. Bird: 8. Guinea pig: 6. How many more means find the difference: 8 − 6 = 2 learners.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar graph go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 2, 4, 6 … Each line is 2 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 2s.

items.q: How many books did Pieter read?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The column for Pieter ends on the line for 12. So the answer is 12 books.

items.q: How many shells did Sibusiso find?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The column for Sibusiso ends halfway between 10 and 12, so it shows 11. So the answer is 11 shells.

items.q: Which column shows the fewest books?
items.e: The column for Pieter is the shortest one. The column for Pieter ends on the line for 4. It shows 4 books.

items.q: How many shells did Nomsa find?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The column for Nomsa ends halfway between 4 and 6, so it shows 5. So the answer is 5 shells.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar graph go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 5, 10, 15 … Each line is 5 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 5s.

items.q: Which column shows 35 cans?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Find 35 on the scale. The column for 3C ends on the line for 35.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar chart go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 2, 4, 6 … Each line is 2 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 2s.

items.q: How many votes did Blue get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Blue bar ends on the line for 35. So the answer is 35 votes.

items.q: How many learners chose curry?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Curry bar ends halfway between 60 and 70, so it shows 65. So the answer is 65 learners.

items.q: How many shells did Lerato find?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Lerato bar ends halfway between 2 and 4, so it shows 3. So the answer is 3 shells.

items.q: How many ash trees are in the park?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Ash bar ends on the line for 10. So the answer is 10 trees.

items.q: Which bar shows 10 votes?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Find 10 on the scale. The Spring bar ends on the line for 10.

items.q: How many learners have a dog?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Dog bar ends halfway between 6 and 8, so it shows 7. So the answer is 7 learners.

items.q: How many Mystery books were borrowed?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Mystery bar ends on the line for 40. So the answer is 40 books.

items.q: Which bar shows the most learners?
items.e: The Walk bar is the longest one. The Walk bar ends on the line for 35. It shows 35 learners.

items.q: How many blackbirds were seen?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Blackbird bar ends halfway between 4 and 6, so it shows 5. So the answer is 5 birds.

items.q: All the angles in a pie chart add up to …
items.e: A pie chart is a whole circle, and the angles at the centre of a circle add up to 360°. (100 is for percentages.)

items.q: A pie chart shows 20 learners. How many degrees stand for each learner?
items.e: The whole circle is 360°. 360 ÷ 20 = 18°, so each learner is 18°. (100 ÷ 20 = 5 uses 100, not 360.)

items.q: A pie chart shows 60 people. How many degrees stand for each person?
items.e: 360 ÷ 60 = 6, so each person is 6°.

items.q: 60 people were asked. 15 chose swimming. What angle should the swimming sector be?
items.e: Each person is 360 ÷ 60 = 6°. 15 × 6 = 90°. (Or: 15 out of 60 is 14, and 14 of 360° = 90°.)

items.q: 24 learners were asked. 8 chose cricket. What angle should the cricket sector be?
items.e: Each learner is 360 ÷ 24 = 15°. 8 × 15 = 120°. (Or: 8 out of 24 is 13, and 13 of 360° = 120°.)

items.q: 30 learners were asked. 9 chose art. What angle should the art sector be?
A sector of a pie chart has an angle of 90°. What fraction of the pie chart is it?
items.e: Compare with the whole circle: 90360 = 14. (90100 uses 100, not 360.)

items.q: A sector of a pie chart has an angle of 120°. What fraction of the pie chart is it?
items.e: 120360 = 13. Three sectors of 120° make 360°.

items.q: A sector of a pie chart has an angle of 45°. What percentage of the pie chart is it?
items.e: 45360 = 18. 18 = 100% ÷ 8 = 12,5%.

items.q: A sector is 16 of a pie chart. What is its angle?
A sector is 25% of a pie chart. What is its angle?
items.e: 25% = 14. 360 ÷ 4 = 90°.

items.q: What is the angle of the Other sector?
What is the angle of the Swimming sector?
How many learners chose soccer?
items.e: Each learner is 360 ÷ 36 = 10°. 150 ÷ 10 = 15 learners.

items.q: 45 learners were asked. 18 chose soccer. What angle should the soccer sector be?
In a pie chart, a sector of 72° stands for 10 people. How many people does the whole pie chart show?
items.e: 72° × 5 = 360°, so the whole pie chart is 5 times as big as the sector: 5 × 10 = 50 people.

items.q: How many more learners walk than come by car?
items.e: Each learner is 360 ÷ 90 = 4°. Walk: 160 ÷ 4 = 40. Car: 80 ÷ 4 = 20. 40 − 20 = 20 learners.

items.q: 40 learners were asked about pets: cat 10, dog 14, fish 6, other 10. What angle should the dog sector be?
Which class has more learners who chose soccer?
items.e: 6A: 23 of 24 = 16 learners. 6B: 13 of 60 = 20 learners. 6B has more, even though its sector is smaller, because 6B has more learners.

items.q: Kyle says, “More learners walk at School A, because its Walk sector is bigger.” Is he right?
items.e: School A: 14 of 120 = 30. School B: 16 of 300 = 50. The sector size only shows the fraction, not the number of learners.

items.q: What is each small square on the salmon scale worth?
items.e: The labels go up by 200. There are 2 small squares between two labels. 200 ÷ 2 = 100 salmon.

items.q: How many salmon were counted in week 3?
items.e: In week 3 the dot is halfway between the lines for 800 and 900. Halfway is 850 salmon.

items.q: In which week were the most salmon counted?
items.e: The highest dot is above week 4: 1 200 salmon.

items.q: How many salmon were counted in week 1?
items.e: In week 1 the dot is halfway between 100 and 200, so 150 salmon.

items.q: In which week were 500 salmon counted?
items.e: 500 is halfway between 400 and 600. The dot there is above week 6. (Week 2 had 400 salmon.)

items.q: Describe the trend in the salmon count over the 7 weeks.
items.e: The count goes up from week 1 to week 4 (1 200 salmon), then goes down to week 7.

items.q: Between which two weeks did the count go up the most?
items.e: Week 2 to 3: 850 − 400 = 450. Week 3 to 4: 1 200 − 850 = 350. Week 1 to 2: 250. The steepest rise is week 2 to week 3, not the part that reaches the top.

items.q: By how much did the count go down from week 4 to week 7?
items.e: Week 4: 1 200. Week 7: 200. 1 200 − 200 = 1 000 salmon. (300 is only week 6 to week 7.)

items.q: What does the flat part from 30 to 40 minutes show?
c: Ayanda biked back to the start
items.e: A flat line means the distance did not change. Ayanda stayed at 5 km for 10 minutes, so she stopped.

items.q: At what time was the temperature 5 °C?
items.e: Find 5 on the scale and go across to the line. The point at 5 °C is above 12:00.

items.q: How tall was the bean plant in week 3?
items.e: The numbers go up in 10s, but each small square is 2 cm. Week 3 is 2 squares above 10: 10 + 2 + 2 = 14 cm. (7 counts the squares as 1 cm each.)

items.q: How much did the plant grow from week 2 to week 5?
items.e: Week 2: 8 cm. Week 5: 22 cm. 22 − 8 = 14 cm. (22 cm is the height, not the growth.)

items.q: Between which two weeks did the plant grow the most?
items.e: The steepest part of the line is from week 2 (8 cm) to week 3 (14 cm): 6 cm. The highest point (week 6) is the tallest, not the fastest growth.

items.q: In which week did the plant first reach 18 cm?
items.e: Find 18 cm on the scale (4 small squares above 10) and go across to the line, then down: week 4.

items.q: How far had Ethan cycled by 10:20?
items.e: Go up from 10:20 to the point. It is on the line for 20, so 20 km.

items.q: Ethan stopped for a rest. When was he resting?
items.e: When Ethan stops, the distance does not change, so the line is flat. From 09:40 to 10:00 it stays at 12 km.

items.q: When was Ethan cycling fastest?
items.e: Fastest means the most distance in the same time: the steepest part. From 10:00 to 10:20 he went 20 − 12 = 8 km. In every other 20 minutes he went 6 km or less.

items.q: How far did Ethan cycle between 09:20 and 10:40?
What was the temperature of the water after 10 minutes?
items.e: The labels go up in 20s, so each square is 10 °C. At 10 minutes the point is halfway between 60 and 70: 65 °C.

items.q: How much did the water cool in the first 5 minutes?
items.e: 0 minutes: 100 °C. 5 minutes: 80 °C. 100 − 80 = 20 °C. After that it cools more slowly.

items.q: Which graph is best to show the height of a sunflower every week for 8 weeks?
c: Bar graph: it shows change over time
Line graph: it shows change over time
items.e: The data is measured again and again over time, so a line graph shows how it changes.

items.q: Which graph is best to show the favourite sport of the learners in your class?
c: Line graph: it shows change over time
Bar graph: it shows change over time
items.e: The data is in separate categories with nothing in between, so use a bar graph. Joining categories with a line makes no sense.

items.q: Which graph is best to show the number of learners in each Grade 6 class at your school?
c: Line graph: it shows change over time
Bar graph: it shows change over time
items.e: The data is in separate categories with nothing in between, so use a bar graph. Joining categories with a line makes no sense.

items.q: Which graph is best to show the number of salmon counted each day during a salmon run?
c: Bar graph: it shows change over time
Line graph: it shows change over time
items.e: The data is measured again and again over time, so a line graph shows how it changes.

items.q: Which graph is best to show how many cars of each colour are in the school parking area?
c: Bar graph: it shows change over time
Line graph: it shows change over time
items.e: The data is in separate categories with nothing in between, so use a bar graph. Joining categories with a line makes no sense.

items.q: Which graph is best to show Lerato’s mass on each birthday from age 6 to age 11?
c: Bar graph: it shows change over time
Line graph: it shows change over time
items.e: The data is measured again and again over time, so a line graph shows how it changes.

items.q: Which graph is best to show how many learners walk, bike, take the bus or come by car to school?
c: Line graph: it shows change over time
Bar graph: it shows change over time
items.e: The data is in separate categories with nothing in between, so use a bar graph. Joining categories with a line makes no sense.

items.q: Which graph is best to show the number of visitors to five BC parks last summer?
c: Bar graph: it shows change over time
Line graph: it shows change over time
items.e: The data is in separate categories with nothing in between, so use a bar graph. Joining categories with a line makes no sense.

items.q: Elna measured the temperature of a cup of hot chocolate every 2 minutes as it cooled. Which graph is best?
c: Bar graph: it shows change over time
Line graph: it shows change over time
items.e: The data is measured again and again over time, so a line graph shows how it changes.

items.q: Ethan showed his class’s favourite sports with this line graph. What is wrong with it?
c: The line should only go up
Sports are categories, so the dots should not be joined
items.e: A line shows change from one point to the next, like over time. Sports have no order and nothing in between them, so Ethan should use a bar graph.

items.q: How many salmon were counted in all 7 weeks?
Naledi says the salmon count doubled from week 1 to week 2. Is she right?
c: No: double 150 is 300, and the count was 400
items.e: Week 1: 150. Double 150 is 300. Week 2: 400, which is more than double.

items.q: Ayanda rested for part of her ride. For how many minutes was she moving?
items.e: The ride lasted 60 minutes. The flat part (30 to 40 minutes) is a 10-minute rest. 60 − 10 = 50 minutes.

items.q: While she was moving, in which 10 minutes did Ayanda bike the shortest distance?
items.e: 20 to 30 minutes: 5 − 4 = 1 km. The other moving parts are 2 km each. From 30 to 40 minutes she was resting, not moving.

items.q: Which graph is best to show how the temperature changes during a day?
items.e: Temperature changes over time. A line graph joins the readings so you can see it rise and fall.

items.q: Which graph is best to show what fraction of a class chose each school dinner?
items.e: A pie chart shows how a whole is split into parts, so you can see each fraction.

items.q: Which sentence about a pie chart is true?
c: A bigger sector always means more people
items.e: A pie chart is a circle, so the angles add up to 360°. A bigger sector is a bigger fraction, but only more people if the totals are the same.

items.q: In which month did the café first sell more ice creams than hot chocolates?
items.e: In March hot chocolate was 90 and ice cream 60, so hot chocolate was still more. In April ice cream was 80 and hot chocolate 60, so April is the first month.

items.q: How many more ice creams than hot chocolates were sold in June?
items.e: Each square is 20. June: ice cream 140, hot chocolate 20. 140 − 20 = 120.

items.q: How many visitors chose giraffes?
items.e: 360 visitors and 360°, so each visitor is 1°. The giraffes sector is 60°, so 60 visitors.
